items.title: Close the --seed non-finite determinism hole in pick()
items.acceptance: --seed Infinity and --seed -Infinity each return the identical aphorism on every run at exit 0, with the same filters applied
items.notes: CONDUCTOR-CONFIRMED defect (kickoff probe: 6 distinct aphorisms in 6 runs, exit 0). Resolution chosen: DETERMINISTIC PICK, not exit 2. Reasoning, judged against the SPEC's own rules: args.js already accepts Infinity as numeric (Number('Infinity') is not NaN) and the Domain rule promises determinism for --seed with no finiteness carve-out, so rejecting it would mean inventing a NEW undocumented validation rule rather than fixing the actual defect — which is that select.js gates its deterministic branch on Number.isFinite while toUint32Seed's IEEE-754 bit-fold already handles +/-Infinity deterministically. NaN stays exit 2 (parseSeedValue already rejects it) and that is correct and unchanged. Doc statement of this resolution belongs to I-3, which is why this item's files_hint is code+test only. NOT flagged route_class core despite playbook L-026: the allocator posture is trickle with allow_premium_pct 0 and opus at 96%, and gear 1's rule is S-effort sonnet builds — deliberately routing a 3-line fix to fable would spend premium the allocator has explicitly zeroed. || VERIFIED cycle 3 by the conductor with checks authored at verification time (the builder never saw them): full test_cmd 52/52 green, end-to-end CLI stability 1-distinct-of-8 for +Inf, -Inf, and +Inf under a --tag filter, and a discriminator that independently re-derived the expected corpus index for each seed (a degenerate index-pin would have passed the stability check alone). NaN contract and the unseeded random branch both confirmed unchanged. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-003-verify-I-1.txt

items.title: Mutation sweep of every documented behavior against the existing suite
items.acceptance: every documented flag and Domain-rule behavior has been mutated at least once against the current suite, and each surviving mutant is recorded with the exact mutation applied and the suite's response
items.notes: MEASUREMENT, not reading (playbook L-031). Behaviors to mutate: seed determinism, unseeded selection, --author case-insensitive matching, --tag membership matching, author+tag AND intersection, empty-set error contract, --list completeness and corpus order, --json single-line shape, the three exit codes, HELP content. Produces a survivor list ONLY. The HOLE-vs-BOUNDARY classification (L-033) is the CONDUCTOR's judgment and is deliberately withheld from this item: a survivor at a genuinely indiscriminable point (unseeded uniformity is the expected example) is the check being correct, and 'hardening' it produces a test that false-rejects honest output. Scratch copies for mutation must be whole-repo-minus-.git, never a hand-enumerated file subset (L-030). || VERIFIED cycle 4 by the conductor. 27 mutants across every catalogued behavior; baseline 52/52. Agent reported 19 KILLED / 7 SURVIVED / 1 EQUIVALENT (M06-EQUIV, dropping .toLowerCase() on the tag ENTRY side, was a no-op because every corpus tag is already lowercase - correctly excluded and replaced by a query-side variant that killed). Conductor re-measurement re-derived all 7 survivors AND a 4-mutant control sample of claimed KILLS from the one-sentence descriptions only, never from the agent's diffs, each in its own whole-repo-minus-.git copy: 11/11 agree, and every survivor carries a conductor-authored observable-difference probe, so none is an equivalent mutant. Classification (conductor, per SPEC Domain rules): 5 HOLE (M07, M12, M13, M14, M21), 1 BOUNDARY (M22 - only the error-message wording changes; exit 2 + clean stdout + stderr message all still hold), 1 DEFERRED to I-3 (M16, --list --json, the surface SPEC lists as an OPEN AMBIGUITY - testing it now would promote today's implementation to a promise and pre-empt I-3). Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-004-verify-I-2a.txt, .swarm/runs/cycle-004-classification.md, .swarm/runs/cycle-004-mutation-sweep.json

items.title: Close HOLE survivors in the CLI-level suite
items.acceptance: each behavior the conductor classified HOLE is covered by a test that fails against its specific mutation, and whose removal lets that same mutation survive
items.notes: Admits tests ONLY for survivors the conductor classified HOLE — never for a surface that merely looks untested. Each test must be proven twice (L-029): failable against its mutation AND attributable, i.e. removing it lets the mutation survive. Planning-time hypotheses, to be settled by I-2a's actual measurement and not assumed: the current --list test asserts only a line-count floor and never order, and the current --json test uses JSON.parse after trim() so a pretty-printed multi-line mutant may still parse. || SETTLED by I-2a (cycle 4). Four assigned HOLE survivors, all observable through the shipped binary: M07 (--tag test must exit 1 - membership, not substring; the corpus has a 'testing' tag and no 'test' tag), M12 (--list line count must equal the corpus size - the existing assertion is a FLOOR of 40 against 50 entries, so dropping an entry passes), M13 (--list first/last line must match corpus order - nothing asserts order today), M14 (--json must be exactly one line - the existing test JSON.parses a trimmed blob, which a pretty-printed object also satisfies). Both planning-time hypotheses in this item were CONFIRMED by measurement. Exact mutations: .swarm/runs/cycle-004-classification.md || VERIFIED cycle 5 by an independent conductor harness (.swarm/runs/cycle-005-verify-I-2b.py, builder never saw it). All four HOLEs proven twice: FAILABLE (mutation applied, suite fails and the designated new test is named) and ATTRIBUTABLE in the strict form (mutation applied + all four new tests skipped -> 52 pass / 0 fail, exactly the pre-sweep baseline, so no pre-existing test was doing the work). A skip-sanity control confirms --test-skip-pattern does not disable the whole run. Suite 52 -> 56 green. Recorded overlap: M12 is length-changing, so it also trips the M13 order test; isolation of M12 alone still leaves fail=1 by design, not by defect.

Conductor harness .swarm/runs/cycle-006-verify-I-2c.py: FAILABLE (M21 -> fail=2, both failures named are the new tests), DENOMINATOR (pattern removes exactly 2 of 58, leaving the 56-test baseline green), ATTRIBUTABLE strict (M21 + new tests filtered -> tests=56 pass=56 fail=0, the pre-cycle baseline to the test), SKIP-SANITY (breaking control mutation under the same pattern -> 7 pre-existing failures). items.title: Settle the four doc/behaviour divergences identically in SPEC.md and README.md
items.acceptance: SPEC.md Domain rules and README.md state in matching wording: how --author matches, what --list does with --seed, what --list --json emits, and how a non-finite --seed behaves; and SPEC.md's OPEN AMBIGUITIES comment is gone rather than left open
items.notes: Four divergences, not three: the I-1 resolution is the fourth and is documented here rather than in I-1, keeping code and prose in separate file scopes. Documentation follows the SHIPPED behavior (--author is substring containment, case-insensitive) rather than changing behavior to match prose — changing the match semantics would be a user-visible behavior change, which the brief forbids. Depends on I-1 so the seed prose describes a resolution that has actually landed. || MEASURED EVIDENCE from I-2a (cycle 4) for divergence (c): mutant M16 rewrote --list --json from NDJSON to a single pretty-printed JSON array and the full 52-test suite stayed green, so that surface is completely unprotected today. It is deliberately NOT being hardened by I-2b/I-2c - no Domain rule describes the combination, so a test would freeze the current implementation and pre-empt this item. Settle the rule here first. || NEW measured evidence (cycle 5): the --list LINE FORMAT ("<text> — <author>", em dash, single line) is now pinned by the M13 order test but is stated by no Domain rule — the rules describe order and completeness of --list, never its rendering. Same shape of gap as M16: a test now enforces something the spec does not promise. I-3 should either write the rule or loosen the assertion to order-only. Do not silently leave the test as the de-facto spec. || CLOSED cycle 7, as a SUPERSET of the three divergences the SPEC named. Conductor rulings, all following SHIPPED behavior: (a) --author is substring containment, case-insensitive; (b) --tag is WHOLE-TAG membership (stated adjacent to (a) so the asymmetry is visible — it is the most confusable thing about the tool); (c) --list accepts a valid --seed and ignores it, exit 0; (d) --list --json is NDJSON, one object per line in corpus order, NOT a JSON array; (e) --list plain form is `<text> — <author>`, em dash U+2014, one line per entry — the cycle-5 gap where a test pinned what no rule promised, resolved by WRITING THE RULE rather than loosening the test, because --list output is a real piped-into contract; (f) --seed accepts every value Number() parses to non-NaN (negative, non-integer, +/-Infinity), all deterministic, NaN alone is exit 2. SPEC's OPEN AMBIGUITIES comment block deleted, not edited. README's brittle '48 tests' count replaced with a description of coverage. || VERIFIED cycle 7 by EXECUTING the shipped binary, never by reading the prose — a docs item whose claims are all behavioral is verifiable the same way a code item is. Harness .swarm/runs/cycle-007-verify-I-3.js (authored at verification time; the agent never saw it): 36/36 checks pass, evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-007-verify-I-3.txt. Four discriminators included so a degenerate implementation could not pass: partial-author result set must EQUAL the full-name set (kills an equality reading of (a)); default 2-line indented output must DIFFER from --list's 1-line form (proves (e) describes two genuinely distinct formats); 7 distinct seeds must reach 7 distinct aphorisms (a determinism check alone is satisfied by an always-same-entry stub); NDJSON first/last line must match corpus[0]/corpus[49] (order, not just parseability). Suite 58/58 green throughout; zero product code touched. CONDUCTOR PRECISION EDIT after the first harness run: the agent's '--list accepts --seed but ignores it' read as though ANY seed value were fine under --list, but the harness EDGE check proved `--list --seed abc` still exits 2. Both files now say 'accepts a valid --seed' and name the parse-failure carve-out. Nothing was weakened to open the gate — the edit made the prose match a measurement that had already passed.

items.title: Align the --help text with the Domain rules I-3 settled
items.acceptance: the HELP string describes --author as a substring match and --tag as a whole-tag match, in wording consistent with SPEC.md Domain rules and README.md, and the suite still passes
items.notes: FOUND cycle 7 while verifying I-3, and deliberately held OUT of I-3's scope: the HELP string lives in src/args.js, a product file, while I-3 was scoped to the two doc files, and mixing them would have broken the pairwise-disjoint file rule. HELP currently says '--author <name>  filter by author (case-insensitive)' and '--tag <tag>  filter by tag (case-insensitive)'. Neither line is FALSE — both flags are case-insensitive — but both are incomplete in exactly the way I-3 just closed elsewhere: they omit that --author is substring containment and --tag is whole-tag, which is the asymmetry users trip over. This is a third documentation surface that still carries the pre-I-3 wording. NOT a behavior change: only the help text's prose moves. Watch for a test that pins HELP content (I-2a mutated HELP and the sweep's notes should be consulted before editing) — if one exists it must be updated in the same item, and a green suite is part of the acceptance. || CLOSED cycle 8 as a SUPERSET of the two divergences this item named. Conductor pre-decided all wording against the shipped source and the landed I-3 rulings; the haiku agent transcribed, it decided nothing. Three HELP lines moved: --author now reads 'filter by author (substring match, case-insensitive)', --tag reads 'filter by tag (whole-tag, case-insensitive)' and sits adjacent so the asymmetry is readable at a glance, and --json reads 'output as JSON (single line, or NDJSON with --list)'. The --json line is the WIDENING, recorded as a decision rather than taken silently: it carried the identical pre-I-3 defect (a documentation surface describing only the non-list case), it lives in the same file and same edit, and drawing the scope line so as to leave one of three known incompletenesses standing in the very file being opened to fix that defect class would have been artificial. HELP-content tests DID exist as the item warned (test/args.test.js: all-flag-names-present, <= 24 lines) - both still pass unmodified, neither needed updating. --seed and --list lines deliberately untouched: they are incomplete but not misleading, and README already carries the detail. || VERIFIED cycle 8. Harness .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-I-7.js, authored at verification time and never shown to the agent; evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-I-7.txt, 35/35 pass. Two things needed proving and reading the diff proves neither. SCOPE: HELP sits in a PRODUCT file, so the harness split src/args.js at the template-literal boundary and byte-compared prologue (216 B) and epilogue (2631 B) against HEAD - identical, so parseArgs and every constant are provably untouched; the literal itself changed 362 -> 397 B, which also proves the item was not a no-op. TRUTH: every new phrase is a claim about runtime behaviour, so each was executed rather than read, with three discriminators - the partial-author result set must EQUAL the full-name set (kills an equality reading of 'substring'), --tag test must exit 1 while --tag testing exits 0 (kills a substring reading of 'whole-tag'), and bare --json must be exactly 1 line while --list --json is 50 (proves the one HELP line names two genuinely distinct shapes, not NDJSON-of-one). End-to-end check confirms the binary prints the EDITED constant, not a stale duplicate. Suite 58/58 green, unchanged from HEAD.

items.title: Harden --list --json now that a Domain rule finally describes it
items.acceptance: a test fails against mutant M16 (--list --json rewritten to emit one pretty-printed JSON array) and, when removed, lets M16 survive the rest of the suite
items.notes: UNBLOCKED BY I-3, and only by I-3. Cycle 4's mutation sweep measured M16 — rewriting --list --json from NDJSON to a single pretty-printed JSON array — as surviving the entire 52-test suite, i.e. that surface is completely unprotected. Cycle 4 classified it DEFERRED rather than HOLE for a specific reason: no Domain rule described the combination, so a test written then would have promoted the day's implementation to a promise and pre-empted the decision I-3 existed to make. I-3 has now MADE that decision (NDJSON, one object per line, corpus order, explicitly not an array), so the surface has a rule and the deferral is spent. Same twice-proven bar as I-2b/I-2c (playbook L-029): failable against M16 specifically, and attributable in the strict form — mutation applied with the new test filtered out must leave the pre-cycle baseline green. The exact M16 mutation is recorded in .swarm/runs/cycle-004-classification.md. M22 stays BOUNDARY and is still not to be hardened. || CLOSED cycle 9. One test added to test/cli.test.js: '--list --json emits newline-delimited JSON, one object per line, in corpus order'. It asserts three things a weaker test would not: line count EQUALS the filtered-set size (an equality, not the floor the pre-existing --list test used), every line parses STANDALONE as a JSON object with text/author/tags (no line of a multi-line array can), and the parsed texts match corpus order. Suite 58 -> 59. || VERIFIED cycle 9 by a conductor harness authored at verification time and never shown to the builder (.swarm/runs/cycle-009-verify-I-8.js, evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-009-verify-I-8.txt, 24/24 pass). Proven twice per L-029: FAILABLE (M16 applied -> fail=1 and the ONLY failing test is the new one) and ATTRIBUTABLE in the strict form (M16 applied + the new test filtered -> tests 58 / pass 58 / fail 0, exactly the pre-cycle baseline the harness re-measured from HEAD rather than took from the builder). Controls: DENOMINATOR (pattern removes exactly 1 of 59 against pristine source, 58 green), SKIP-SANITY (an unrelated mutation still fails under the same pattern), and MUTATION-APPLIED on every scratch copy -- the last one matters most, because a mutation that silently failed to apply would make the ATTRIBUTABLE check pass VACUOUSLY, which is a pass-shaped false result. Three DISCRIMINATORS the new test also kills: a COMPACT single-line JSON array (still valid JSON, still every entry in order), REVERSED NDJSON order, and TRUNCATED NDJSON with the last entry dropped. The latter two also trip the pre-existing M12/M13 --list tests, which is the expected length/order overlap cycle 5 recorded, not a defect -- the claim is that the NEW test is among the failures, and it is. Product tree byte-identical to HEAD (bin/aphorism.js, src/args.js, src/select.js, src/corpus.js all compared against HEAD); git diff --name-only HEAD = test/cli.test.js alone. The I-2 hardening thread is now complete: every HOLE survivor from cycle 4's sweep is closed, and M22 remains BOUNDARY and unhardened as classified.

items.title: Corpus attribution triage (umbrella — decomposed cycle 10 into I-4a + I-4b)
items.acceptance: a written risk-ranked list names the corpus entries most likely to carry a wrong or unverifiable attribution with a stated reason each, and no file in the repo describes the corpus as audited, verified, or fact-checked
items.notes: TRIAGE, never an audit — nothing here can be confirmed without sources this run cannot reach, and the deliverable is explicitly a list for a human to settle (KI-2, T-006). Rank by internally-observable risk signals only: folklore maxims historically credited to several different people, wording that looks paraphrased or compressed rather than verbatim, entries already hedged as Anonymous (lowest risk, already honest), and entries traceable to a specific well-documented publication (lower risk). The stress-test's demo-embarrassment lens put this ABOVE the test items in value: a programming-aphorism CLI with misattributed quotes fails in exactly the way a green suite cannot see. || DECOMPOSED cycle 10 into I-4a and I-4b, per the cycle-9 handoff's stated preference for S-effort slices over accepting one M-effort exception under gear 1. The split is NOT by risk band, which would have been circular — you cannot slice by a ranking the work exists to produce. It is by KIND of claim: I-4b is the ranked judgment artifact (what is likely wrong), I-4a is a mechanical repo sweep (does any file overclaim). Those need different evidence and different verification, which is what makes the seam real. This umbrella closes when I-4a lands; id retired from direct execution, not dropped. || UMBRELLA CLOSED cycle 11 — both acceptance clauses verified, each with its own evidence. Clause 1 (risk-ranked list with a stated reason each) closed by I-4b cycle 10. Clause 2 (no file describes the corpus as audited/verified/fact-checked) closed by I-4a cycle 11 and verified by a REPO-WIDE sweep over all 9 product files, not just the edited one. Method note worth keeping: the first sweep returned "0 hits" and was DISCARDED rather than banked, because its negative control did not fire — the detector could not even find the text I had just deleted ("honest // attribution" defeated \s+ across the comment marker). The rewritten detector fires on the exact old header plus two synthetic overclaims, and only then was its 0-hit result admitted as evidence. A zero from a detector that has not been shown to be capable of a one is not a zero.

items.title: Sweep the repo for language that overclaims the corpus as audited or verified
items.acceptance: no file in the repo describes the corpus as audited, verified, fact-checked, or its attributions as honest/correct, and any such wording is replaced with an accurate description that points at docs/corpus-attribution-triage.md
items.notes: The other half of I-4's acceptance clause. CONDUCTOR-SCOUTED cycle 10, not yet executed: a grep across README.md, REPORT.md and src/ found REPORT.md already honest (it states the attributions are unaudited and KI-2 open), but src/corpus.js carries a header comment claiming 'honest attribution' and that uncertain entries 'are attributed to Anonymous rather than guessing a famous name'. I-4b measured that claim as false in at least 8 places: exactly one of 50 entries is hedged to Anonymous, while eight carry HIGH-risk attributions to named people. So this is a real overclaim in a PRODUCT file, not a paperwork tidy. Ordered AFTER I-4b deliberately — the triage supplies the evidence for what the replacement wording may honestly say, and doing it first would have meant writing the comment twice. Conductor-executed and S-effort: it is a prose edit to a product file, which by the cycle-8 precedent must be gated by byte-comparing everything outside the edited comment against HEAD. || DONE cycle 11, conductor-executed. Two edits, both prose: (1) src/corpus.js header — the claim "honest attribution" and the policy sentence "where the true author is uncertain ... the entry is attributed to Anonymous rather than guessing a famous name" were REMOVED, not softened, because I-4b measured them false (1 of 50 hedged to Anonymous vs 8 HIGH-risk entries all naming famous people: Knuth, Karlton, Dijkstra, Beck, Wheeler, Hopper, Stroustrup, Kay). Restating a policy the file does not follow, in weaker words, would still have been fiction. Replacement states attribution is UNVERIFIED and points at the triage. (2) README.md gained an "## Attribution" section — this one is an ADDITION, not a correction: the README did not overclaim, it was simply silent, leaving the triage doc undiscoverable to the only reader who matters. Gated 19/19 incl. 3 negative controls; corpus data deep-equal to HEAD; suite 59/59.

items.title: Risk-ranked attribution triage document for the 50-entry corpus
items.acceptance: a written risk-ranked list names the corpus entries most likely to carry a wrong or unverifiable attribution, with an entry-specific stated reason for each of all 50 entries, and never presents itself as an audit
items.notes: TRIAGE, never an audit (KI-2, T-006). Dispatched as ONE sonnet Agent, file scope exactly docs/corpus-attribution-triage.md, network use explicitly forbidden — the deliverable's whole value depends on it being honest about resting on recall alone. || VERIFIED cycle 10. The hard problem: a triage is a JUDGMENT artifact, so no command's exit code can prove it right, and the usual gate has nothing to bite on. Two-part answer. (1) Everything mechanically provable was proven by harness .swarm/runs/cycle-010-verify-I-4b.js (16/16, evidence .swarm/runs/cycle-010-verify-I-4b.txt): all 50 entries covered exactly once and keyed to the corpus by TWO independent columns (author verbatim + text prefix, so a shifted or invented row cannot pass), fixed risk/signal vocabularies, non-degeneracy (>=3 bands, no band over 60%, 7 distinct signals), 50 distinct non-boilerplate reasons, the self-hedged Anonymous entry anchored to LOW, product tree byte-identical to HEAD and suite 59/59 green. Two NEGATIVE CONTROLS prove the checks can fail: a corrupted table (row dropped + author swapped) is rejected, and a hypothetical all-MEDIUM table fails non-degeneracy. (2) The substantive claim was measured against a ranking SEALED BEFORE DISPATCH (.swarm/runs/cycle-010-precommit.md): the agent's HIGH band {0,3,10,27,38,39,45,48} contains 4 of the 5 sealed Tier A entries, and independently found 4 the conductor had not ranked HIGH. || CONDUCTOR ADDENDUM appended to the document, marked as separately authored: the four places the two independent derivations DISAGREED, recorded as disagreements between two unverified opinions rather than as corrections. Chief among them, row #45 asserts that Stroustrup's FAQ disclaims the foot-gun quote while the conductor recalls the opposite — that row is the only one in the table making a checkable claim about what a primary source says, so it was moved to the top of the human's queue precisely because the two passes conflict. Also added: the #25 Postel paraphrase the table rated LOW and missed.

items.title: Consolidate the tag taxonomy so every advertised tag has a real pool
items.acceptance: No tag reachable via --tag returns a fixed single entry: every tag present in the corpus has >= 3 entries, achieved by RETAGGING existing aphorisms (folding singletons into neighbours), not by adding aphorisms. --tag remains whole-tag case-insensitive and the suite stays green.
items.notes:
Source: cycle-14 taste pass, finding 1 (notable). Conductor-verified: 21 of 37 tags hold exactly one entry and 30 of 37 hold <=2, so --tag naming and --tag caching return the identical Phil Karlton line on every invocation forever (8/8 pulls, 1 distinct output). The taste agent reported 23 singletons; the true figure is 21 (harness C1c) — the finding survives on corrected numbers. NOT picked at gear 1: M-effort, and gear 1 admits S-effort builds only. Judgment flag for whoever picks it up: retagging silently changes what existing --tag queries return, which is a behaviour change to a shipped contract even though it adds no feature — the Domain rules should be re-read before it lands.

items.title: Publish the tag vocabulary in README and --help

Conductor-verified: --help is 10 lines and names zero tags (C4a); README names 2 of 37 tags and only as inline examples (C4b); guessing costs real misses — --tag bugs exits 1 while the corpus spells it debugging (C4c). Squarely in scope for an improvement run (documentation) and S-effort, so it is admissible at gear 1. items.title: Surface the quote-of-the-day recipe in the README usage examples
items.acceptance: README usage examples include the date-seeded one-liner (node bin/aphorism.js --seed $(date +%Y%m%d)) with a one-line explanation that it is stable all day and changes tomorrow. The claim must be true of the shipped binary, not just plausible.
items.notes: Source: cycle-14 taste pass, finding 4 (minor). Conductor-verified that the recipe actually works before filing it: three consecutive date seeds are each stable across 3 runs and yield 3 distinct quotes (C5a, C5b), and the README currently shows only the fixture-shaped --tag simplicity --seed 42 with no date recipe (C5c). Best value-per-effort item on the board: it costs one README line and converts an existing, already-verified flag into the reason a user comes back tomorrow, without adding a feature or any rotation state. This is the taste pass paying for itself in scope. CYCLE 15 VERIFIED: landed as a single README line inside the usage-examples fence -- `node bin/aphorism.js --seed $(date +%Y%m%d)      # same aphorism all day; changes at local midnight`. Conductor harness .swarm/runs/cycle-015-verify-T-010.{js,txt}: 19/19 with 4 negative controls. The line was pasted verbatim into bash and its output matched the today-seeded run byte for byte (A6/A7), so the recipe is proven against the shipped binary rather than read. Scope clean: 1 insertion, 0 deletions, Flags table and every fenced section byte-identical.

items.title: Tighten the quote-of-the-day recipe's change claim to match the measured behaviour
items.acceptance: The README's date-seed recipe comment does not imply the aphorism always differs from one day to the next. Reworded so it stays true on the days it repeats, without adding a sentence of hedging clutter to a one-line example -- the comment must remain a single trailing comment on one line.
items.notes: Source: conductor verification gate, cycle 15 (harness check A4/A9). MEASURED, not suspected: sweeping 365 consecutive date seeds against the shipped binary, 11 of 364 consecutive-day pairs return the SAME aphorism (~3%) -- the seed always changes at local midnight, but the selection it maps to does not. First few: 20261015->20261016, 20261107->20261108, 20270121->20270122. Over a year all 50 corpus entries appear. The shipped comment reads 'same aphorism all day; changes at local midnight', whose subject is ambiguous: read as 'the aphorism changes at local midnight' it is false about 11 days a year. It is NOT a gate failure -- A9 passed, since the phrasing carries no unhedged every-day-different promise, and the clause it does make unambiguously (local midnight, not UTC) is exactly right. Filed rather than absorbed because this run's identity is closing doc/behaviour divergences (I-3) and sweeping overclaiming language (I-4a); prose this run ADDS is held to the same standard. Deliberately not fixed by the conductor: the conductor authored the gate that found it, and fixing it inline would be coding to its own check. CLOSED cycle 16: reworded to "same aphorism all day; seed refreshes at local midnight" -- the change-clause now names the SEED as its subject, so the false reading is unavailable. Conductor gate 20/20 with 5 negative controls; the two factual claims the comment makes were each machine-checked (one-seed-per-local-day and one-aphorism-per-seed for clause 1; the local-midnight boundary, plus that the same instants do NOT cross a UTC boundary, for clause 2). Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-016-verify-T-011.txt

items.title: readme-tags guard: prose-list coverage is keyed to one exact sentence
items.acceptance: The invented-tag check keeps working when the single-entry list is reworded: rewriting the lead-in sentence "The remaining N tags appear exactly once:" to any other phrasing must still cause a corpus-absent tag name in that list to fail the suite. Prove it with a reworded README plus a bogus tag, and confirm the failing assertion is the tag-existence one by name, not merely that something went red.
items.notes: Source: conductor gate check F10, cycle 17 (INFO probe, not a gate failure -- the shipped README is correct and fully watched today). test/readme-tags.test.js finds the single-entry list by matching the literal /The remaining \d+ tags appear exactly once: (.+?)\./. Measured: rewording that lead-in and inserting `zzzbogus` left the tag-existence test SILENT -- the only failure came from a different assertion (the single-entry count), which would disappear too if the count sentence moved with it. So the guard degrades quietly under an edit a future docs cycle could plausibly make. VALUE_LOOP note, recorded rather than hidden: no user of the CLI would ever notice this, so it does not clear the "would the target user notice?" ratchet as a feature. It is filed because this is a hardening run and a guard that can go quiet is the exact failure class this run exists to remove -- it competes for a slot on that basis, not on user-visible value. RESOLVED cycle 18: extraction made structural (fenced code blocks stripped from the Tag vocabulary section, then every backtick-quoted [a-z]+ token in what remains is a tag claim, via the file's existing extractTagsFromReadme helper). Conductor gate 24/24 (.swarm/runs/cycle-018-verify-T-012.txt). Kill is ATTRIBUTED: the same reworded-lead-in + bogus-tag mutation is missed by HEAD's test file (D1) and caught by the new one, while the un-reworded mutation was caught by both (D2) -- so the regression really was reword-specific and the fix is what closes it. Routed sonnet, not the haiku recorded at plan time: routing is pick-time and kind:fix never demotes below sonnet at gear 1.

items.title: Mutation sweep: which README claims can go false without the suite noticing
items.acceptance: every factual claim README.md makes about the product or the corpus has been mutated at least once against the current suite, and each surviving mutant is recorded with the exact mutation applied and the suite's response
items.notes: MEASUREMENT, not reading (L-031). Cycle 4's sweep (I-2a) predates every documentation guard this run built, and the README has since grown a Tag vocabulary section (T-009), a date-seed recipe (T-010/T-011) and an Attribution section (I-4a). The question is not whether the README is true today -- the conductor measured every number in it as correct before dispatch -- but which claims could silently STOP being true. This matters concretely because T-007 (retagging) is live on the backlog and would falsify most of the tag numbers at once. HOLE-vs-BOUNDARY classification withheld from the agent (L-033); it is the conductor's judgment. || VERIFIED cycle 19. Agent measured 21 mutants: 9 KILLED, 12 SURVIVED. Conductor harness .swarm/runs/cycle-019-verify-T-013.{js,txt} re-derived 8 survivors and a 4-mutant control sample of claimed KILLS from the one-sentence descriptions ONLY, never from the agent's diffs, each in its own whole-repo-minus-.git copy: 37/37, full agreement, plus one survivor the agent never tested (V6). Sealed pre-commitment .swarm/runs/cycle-019-precommit.md, written before dispatch, predicted all 12 survivors correctly. Controls that make the result sound: PRISTINE (unmutated copy must be 65/65 -- it FIRED on the harness's first run and exposed a parser bug that had silently turned every verdict into KILLED), APPLIED per mutant (a mutation that fails to apply makes SURVIVED vacuous), and PAIRED positive controls so each Class-A finding is ATTRIBUTED rather than merely observed. Classification: .swarm/runs/cycle-019-classification.md -- 10 HOLE, 3 BOUNDARY, collapsing into follow-ups T-014..T-017.

items.title: Make the README tag-table guard bidirectional and band-aware
items.acceptance: Deleting an entire tag row from either README count table fails the suite, and moving a row into a band whose stated range its count does not satisfy fails the suite. Both must be proven twice per L-029: failable against the specific mutation, and attributable -- removing the new assertion lets that mutation survive the rest of the suite.
items.notes: Source: T-013 survivors A7 and A8, cycle 19. The ONLY Class A finding in the sweep -- a guard that exists, passes, and is blind in one direction, which is the exact T-012 failure class this run has already fixed once. Both are ATTRIBUTED, not merely observed: V1 (row deleted) survives while V1b (wrong count, same table) kills, and V2 (row moved to the wrong band, count untouched) survives while V2b (same row, wrong count) kills. So the count check is provably live and provably one-directional. Highest-value follow-up because T-007 (retagging) is live on the backlog and would walk straight into it. Exact mutations pre-specified in .swarm/runs/cycle-019-classification.md, so the failability targets do not need re-deriving. VERIFIED cycle 20: 17/17 conductor gate checks (.swarm/runs/cycle-020-verify-T-014.txt). Both acceptance mutations killed AND attributed using mutations the builder never ran (I deleted the `debugging` row from the 5+ table; it had proved A7 on `testing` in the other table). Residual filed as T-018.

items.title: Guard every corpus-derived number in the Tag vocabulary section
items.acceptance: Changing any of 'N tags appear on 2 or more entries', 'N tags have a robust pool (5+ entries)', 'N tags appear 2-4 times', or the second statement of the single-entry count ('the remaining N appear on exactly one entry') to a wrong number fails the suite. Keyed to the numbers and their meaning, not to one exact sentence -- rewording a lead-in must not make a check go quiet.
items.notes: Source: T-013 survivors A9, A10, A11 and the conductor-original V6, cycle 19. These integers are the same kind as the two that ARE guarded ('37 distinct tags', '21 appear exactly once'); nothing distinguishes them except which sentences someone happened to write a regex for. V6 is the sharpest: the single-entry count is stated TWICE in README.md and guarded ONCE -- V6 (line 55 phrasing) survives while V6b (line 81 phrasing) kills, so the README can contradict itself about the same number and stay green. The agent's sweep never tested it; it came from the conductor harness. NOTE the standing hazard from T-012: do not key the new assertions to literal lead-in sentences, or this item recreates the very defect cycle 18 removed. || VERIFIED cycle 21, 28/29 conductor gate checks (.swarm/runs/cycle-021-verify-T-015.txt); the one failure was the SCOPE.SCRATCH housekeeping control, not an acceptance clause -- see below. Two tests added, 116 insertions / 0 deletions, suite 66 -> 68. PRE-DISPATCH BASELINE (.swarm/runs/cycle-021-baseline.txt) measured the blindness rather than assuming it: all four claims SURVIVED at 66/66/0, while the paired controls V6b (line-81 phrasing of the SAME integer 21) and C0 (the 37 total) both KILLED -- so the existing guards were provably live and provably blind to exactly these four. All four proven twice per L-029 with conductor mutations the builder never saw: I used OFF-BY-ONE errors in both directions (16->17, 21->20, 4->3, 12->13) where the builder had used 99/88/77/55, and each FAILABLE run names one of the two NEW tests while each ATTRIBUTABLE run returns exactly 66/66/0. R2 is the check no acceptance clause asked for and the one that matters most for T-007: I mutated the CORPUS (one entry gains tag `performance`, 4 -> 5) and updated the README to the new TRUE numbers -- the suite stayed GREEN at 68/68, which a hardcoded 4/12 could not do; the paired stale-README half fails at 3 tests. R1 (T-012 hazard) measured clean in both directions: all four lead-ins reworded with digits intact stays green, and a wrong cardinality under the reworded prose still kills. N3 confirms the two statements of `21` are guarded INDEPENDENTLY -- mutating the line-81 phrasing alone fires the pre-existing test and leaves the new ones quiet. SCOPE.SCRATCH: the builder deleted its mutation copies but left an EMPTY .swarm/scratch directory; measured at 0 files inside, no content leaked, conductor removed it (cycle-9 pattern, KI-7). Recorded as a failed control rather than re-run to a manufactured green. Residual filed as T-019.

items.title: Guard the README's cross-file and on-disk claims
items.acceptance: The corpus-size figure in the Attribution section ('ranks all N entries') must match corpus.length; the HIGH-risk count ('N are rated HIGH') must match docs/corpus-attribution-triage.md; and every path named in the Layout block must exist on disk. Each proven twice per L-029.
items.notes: Source: T-013 survivors C1, C2, C6, cycle 19. All three are machine-checkable against something real (corpus length, another file in the repo, the filesystem) rather than against prose, which is why they are HOLE and the Flags/Exit-code table survivors are BOUNDARY. C6 is the cheapest real protection on the board: a file rename currently makes the Layout block lie with nothing noticing. C2 is the weakest of the three -- the triage doc is stable and human-owned -- and may honestly be dropped if it proves fiddly to parse; say so rather than forcing it. || VERIFIED cycle 22, 23/23 conductor gate checks (.swarm/runs/cycle-022-verify-T-016.txt), zero failures. All three claims stayed in scope and none was dropped: C2 proved machine-parseable (the triage table holds 50 rows, ids 0-49 distinct, HIGH 8 / MEDIUM 16 / LOW 26), so the item’s standing permission to drop C2 honestly was not needed and dropping it would have needed a reason I did not have. PRE-DISPATCH BASELINE (.swarm/runs/cycle-022-baseline.txt) MEASURED the blindness rather than inheriting cycle 19’s survivor list: C1, C2 and C6 all SURVIVED at 68/68/0 while the paired control C0 (37 distinct tags -> 38, a claim the suite provably DOES guard) KILLED at 68/67/1 -- so the existing suite was provably live and provably blind to exactly these three. Three tests added, 186 insertions / 0 deletions, suite 68 -> 71. All three proven twice per L-029 using conductor mutations the builder never saw, deliberately in the opposite direction or on a different target: 50->51 (UP, where the builder used 49 DOWN), 8->7 (DOWN, where the builder used 9 UP), and bin/aphorism.js plus the test/ directory entry (where the builder used src/select.js). Every FAILABLE run names the matching new test; every ATTRIBUTABLE run returns exactly 68/68/0, the pre-cycle baseline. The decisive checks are the three R2 TRACKS/STALE pairs, which no acceptance clause asked for and which are the only form that separates a guard derived from the real artifact from one hardcoding today’s numbers: adding a 51st corpus entry AND updating the README consistently stays GREEN at 71/71 while the stale half fails naming C1; flipping a triage row MEDIUM->HIGH AND updating the README stays GREEN while the stale half fails naming C2; creating a real new file AND adding its Layout line stays GREEN while a Layout line for a file that was never created fails naming C6. A hardcoded guard fails all three TRACKS halves. R1 (the T-012 prose-keying hazard) measured clean in both directions: prose reworded with digits and paths intact stays green, and reworded prose plus a wrong number still kills naming C1. R5 confirms a parse miss is LOUD, never a silent pass -- deleting the whole Attribution section fails 2 tests by name, and replacing the Layout fence with prose fails C6. Residual filed as T-020.

items.title: Check the --list format literal against the binary's real output
items.acceptance: Changing the separator in the README's --list format literal (`<text> — <author>`, U+2014) so it no longer matches what the shipped binary actually prints fails the suite. Proven twice per L-029.
items.notes: Source: T-013 survivor C5, cycle 19. The interesting property that makes this a HOLE rather than a BOUNDARY: the README states the format BOTH as English prose ('text, space, EM DASH, space, author') AND as a literal inside backticks. Asserting against the literal is a literal-vs-behaviour check, so it freezes no wording -- the prose sentence stays free to be reworded. Do NOT write the check against the English sentence; that would be the C3/C4/C7 boundary mistake. VERIFIED cycle 23: 17/18 conductor gate checks green on the first harness run and 18/18 after two HARNESS defects were repaired (TAP reporter for by-name failure attribution; name-filter denominator), plus 4/4 on the TRACKS addendum. The item claim is carried by C5/C5b: two README-literal mutations the builder never used (pipe separator, spaces removed) each fail exactly one test BY NAME, and each SURVIVES at the pre-cycle baseline 71/71/0 with that test filtered out. Binary-side mutations (separator, order, length) also name T-017 but are NOT attributable to it -- the pre-existing test "--list preserves corpus order (first and last line match)" already covers the binary alone. T-017 unique contribution is therefore the README-literal side of the comparison, which is exactly what survivor C5 named.

items.title: Let the band-table parser tolerate a blank line between a heading and its table
items.acceptance: Inserting a blank line between a band heading and its `| Tag | Count |` table (idiomatic markdown, and it makes no README claim false) leaves the suite green, while a row deletion under that reformatted heading still fails. Proven twice per L-029.
items.notes: Source: conductor probe N3, cycle 20 -- .swarm/runs/cycle-020-verify-T-014.txt. extractBandTablesFromReadme requires the heading at line i and the table header at i+1, so a blank line makes the band undetectable. IMPORTANT and the reason this is LOW priority, not a repeat of T-012: the guard does NOT go quiet. Its bands.length>0 sanity assertion fires and the suite FAILS LOUDLY, naming the parse as the cause -- measured, reformat alone gives fail 1, and reformat+row-deletion is still KILLED. So this is a false REJECTION of an honest edit, the safe direction, not a silent hole. Fix shape: skip blank lines between the heading and the table header rather than requiring adjacency. || VERIFIED cycle 27, 24/25 conductor gate checks (.swarm/runs/cycle-027-verify-T-018.txt); the single red is analysed below and is proven NOT to belong to this item. Fix landed as authored: the header-row lookup skips blank lines forward from i+1 and requires the FIRST non-blank line to be the header row, so no later table can be grafted onto a heading that has none; row collection moves from a fixed i+3 to headerIdx+2. +18/-2 lines, one file, no product byte touched, no assertion removed (S1-S5). || THE PRE-DISPATCH BASELINE FOUND WHAT THE ITEM TEXT DID NOT (.swarm/runs/cycle-027-baseline.txt), and it changed what the acceptance had to mean. Cycle 20 recorded 'reformat+row-deletion is still KILLED' and read that as the guard still working. Re-measured at the current 73-test suite, reformat+row-deletion (B4) fails with the IDENTICAL signature as reformat ALONE (B1): 73/72/1 naming only the T-019 union test. The deleted row is MASKED -- the whole band is invisible, so the suite is reporting the parse failure, not the deletion. A fix that merely made the reformat green while leaving detection broken would have satisfied the acceptance clause exactly as written. The gate therefore demanded more than the clause: under a reformatted heading a row deletion must produce the SAME signature as a row deletion with no reformat at all. It does -- A7 (no reformat) and A8 (reformat) both land 73/71/2 with the identical two failing test names, including the band-contents assertion that was absent from the masked form. Detection is genuinely restored, not merely un-reddened. || GREEN half proven twice per L-029 and ATTRIBUTED by the cycle-25 method (test count is unchanged at 73, so --test-skip-pattern has nothing to filter; the copy's test file is reverted to git HEAD instead): A1/A2/A3 green at 73/73/0 for the 5+ table, the 2-4 table and both at once, while A1b/A2b/A3b apply the identical README to HEAD's parser and are REJECTED (73/72/1, 73/72/1, 73/70/3). Control C3 proves the reversion mechanism itself is sound (HEAD's parser on an unmutated README is green), so the attribution measures the fix rather than the swap. || THREE EDGE CASES THE BUILDER REPORTED AS UNEXECUTED were executed by the gate and all hold: three consecutive blank lines (A4), a whitespace-only line (A5) and a tab-only line (A6) each stay green. So does the constraint-6 scenario it reasoned through but never ran: a decoy line carrying a band-shaped digit token, blank line, then the real heading and table does NOT steal the table (A11, 73/73/0). The builder's honest uncertainty list is the third cycle running (cf. T-020 c22, T-021 c23) to convert directly into measured checks. || LOUDNESS re-proven in four directions, since a tolerance fix's whole risk is going quiet: a wrong stated band count under a reformat still fails (A10), a heading followed by prose rather than a table still fails rather than silently attaching a later table (A12), the zero-band sanity assertion is still reachable (A13), and negative control C2 proves the harness can produce a red at all.

items.title: Guard against an entire band table disappearing from the Tag vocabulary section
items.acceptance: Deleting an entire band table (its heading AND all its rows) from the Tag vocabulary section fails the suite. Proven twice per L-029: failable against that specific deletion, and attributable -- removing the new assertion lets the same deletion survive the rest of the suite.
items.notes: Source: conductor probe N2, cycle 21 -- .swarm/runs/cycle-021-verify-T-015.txt. MEASURED, not suspected: removing the whole '12 tags appear 2-4 times:' heading and its 12-row table leaves the suite GREEN at 68/68. This is the T-014/A7 blindness one level up. T-014 made each band table's row set bidirectional, and T-015 made each band heading's stated cardinality checkable, but BOTH iterate only over the bands that are PRESENT -- a band that stops being claimed at all is not iterated, so nothing notices. Every stated fact remains true; the README has simply gone quiet about 12 tags. Fix shape: derive the expected PARTITION of bands from the corpus (or assert the union of all band tables' rows equals the set of tags with count >= 2) instead of only validating the bands that happen to appear. Note the interaction with T-018: whatever mechanism is chosen must still fail LOUD rather than quiet when the section is reformatted, and must not be keyed to lead-in prose (T-012 hazard). Lower priority than T-016/T-017 because a whole table vanishing is a far less likely edit than the single-row and cross-file cases those cover, and unlike A7 it is not on the path of T-007 (retagging edits rows, it does not delete tables). CYCLE 23 NOTE: this item text says "lower priority than T-016/T-017" while carrying priority 5 against their 6. Both of those are now done, so the contradiction is moot and the number is left as written rather than edited -- T-019 is genuinely next on value, being the only remaining SILENT hole on the board (the README goes quiet and nothing notices). The three remaining guard items (T-018, T-020, T-021) are all LOUD false rejections, i.e. the safe direction. || VERIFIED cycle 24, 21/23 conductor gate checks (.swarm/runs/cycle-024-verify-T-019.txt); both failures are analysed below and neither is an acceptance clause. One test added, +65/-0, suite 72 -> 73. PRE-DISPATCH BASELINE (.swarm/runs/cycle-024-baseline.txt) re-MEASURED the blindness at the current 72-test suite rather than inheriting cycle 21's 68-test figure, and turned up a fact cycle 21 did not record: deleting EITHER band table alone survives 72/72, but deleting BOTH kills at 72/70/2 because the pre-existing `bands.length > 0` sanity assertion fires only at zero bands. The defect was therefore all-or-nothing, which is what the fix had to address. Mechanism is corpus-derived: the union of rows across whatever band tables are present must cover every corpus tag with count >= 2 -- it asserts nothing about how many bands exist or where their boundaries fall. Both acceptance mutations proven twice per L-029 with conductor mutations run independently of the builder's report: deleting the 2-4 table and deleting the 5+ table each fail naming T-019 AND NOTHING ELSE, and each SURVIVES at exactly the pre-cycle baseline 72/72/0 with that one test filtered out. The decisive checks are the two R-pairs, which no acceptance clause asked for and which are the only form that separates a corpus-derived guard from one hardcoding today's two bands and today's 16 multi-entry tags. R1: promoting `yagni` from a 1-entry to a 2-entry tag IN THE CORPUS and updating the README consistently stays GREEN at 73/73 (a hardcoded 16-tag union cannot do that), while the stale half fails at 73/68/5 with T-019 among the named failures. R2 is the sharper one and uses a layout that does not exist in this repo today: restructuring the section into THREE bands (10+, 5-9, 2-4), corpus untouched and every stated fact still true, is NOT falsely rejected (73/73) -- and deleting the MIDDLE of those three bands fails naming T-019 alone and is attributable at 72/72/0. That middle-band mutation is the one the builder never had available, because with two band tables still standing the zero-band sanity assertion provably cannot be what fires. Residual filed as T-022.

items.title: Make the Attribution count extraction robust to digits reordered within one clause
items.acceptance: Rewording the Attribution sentence so that a different CORRECT digit sits nearer the HIGH marker than the HIGH count itself -- e.g. `8 of the 50 entries carry a rating of HIGH` -- leaves the suite GREEN, while the same reworded prose carrying a WRONG HIGH count still fails. Proven twice per L-029.
items.notes: Source: conductor probe N1, cycle 22 -- .swarm/runs/cycle-022-verify-T-016.txt. MEASURED, not suspected: rewriting the Attribution aside as `covers every entry. 8 of the 50 entries carry a rating of HIGH, and it says what would settle each one.` -- with every number still TRUE -- fails the suite at 71/70/1, naming the C2 test. Cause: extractNearestPrecedingCount splits the section on em/en dashes and then takes the digit run NEAREST BEFORE the marker within that clause; with the dashes gone the whole paragraph collapses into one clause, and in that word order 50 sits nearer to HIGH than 8 does. The builder flagged exactly this edge case in its own report rather than hiding it, which is the only reason it was probed -- an honest uncertainty report converted directly into a measured backlog item. IMPORTANT, and the reason this is LOW value rather than a repeat of T-012: the guard does NOT go quiet. It fails LOUD and names the claim, so a maintainer who trips it is told exactly what happened. This is a false REJECTION of an honest edit -- the safe direction -- and it gets the same classification T-018 got at cycle 20 for the same reason. Fix shape: bind the digit to its marker by proximity in BOTH directions within the clause, or match the two claims as a pair (`N ... entries` and `M ... HIGH`), rather than assuming the README will keep using dash-delimited asides. Whatever is chosen must still fail LOUD on a genuine parse miss (R5, verified this cycle) and must not be keyed to lead-in prose (the standing T-012 hazard).

items.title: Let the --list-behaviour section locator tolerate a reformatted heading
items.acceptance: Dropping the backticks from the "### `--list` behaviour" heading (an honest markdown reformat that makes no README claim false, and that leaves the format literal and the binary untouched) leaves the suite GREEN, while a mutated format literal under that same reformatted heading still FAILS. Proven twice per L-029. || ACCEPTANCE AMENDED BY MEASUREMENT, cycle 28 -- the clause above is necessary but PROVABLY NOT SUFFICIENT, and a fix satisfying only it was rejected this cycle. Two additions, both measured, not supposed. (1) FAIL FOR THE RIGHT REASON: at HEAD, reformat-alone and reformat-plus-mutated-literal produce the IDENTICAL signature 73/72/1 naming the same test (baseline B1 vs B3), because the heading parse failure MASKS the literal mutation. So 'still FAILS' is already true at HEAD and cannot distinguish a fix that restores detection from one that does not. The red half must therefore fail with a SEPARATOR-MISMATCH message, not a heading-parse message. (2) NO FIRST-MATCH THEFT: the fix must not let an EARLIER '### ' heading that happens to carry both the --list token and the word 'behaviour' capture the section. Measured consequence of getting this wrong is a SILENT HOLE, not a loud rejection -- see notes.
items.notes:
Source: conductor probe N1, cycle 23 -- .swarm/runs/cycle-023-verify-T-017.txt. MEASURED, not suspected: rewriting the heading as "### --list behaviour" fails the suite at fail=1, naming the T-017 test. Cause: getListBehaviourSection anchors on /^### `--list` behaviour\s*$/m, so the backticks are load-bearing in the locator. The BUILDER FLAGGED THIS EXACT CASE in its own "things I was unsure about" section before it was probed -- the second cycle running (cf. T-020 at cycle 22) where an honest uncertainty note converted straight into a measured item. IMPORTANT, and why this is LOW value rather than a T-012 repeat: the guard does NOT go quiet. Its assert fires with the message "README must have a \"### `--list` behaviour\" section", so a maintainer who trips it is told exactly what happened. Same safe-direction classification as T-018 (cycle 20) and T-020 (cycle 22). Fix shape: match the heading on the token --list plus the word behaviour, tolerating optional backticks, rather than requiring the exact backticked form. Whatever is chosen must still fail LOUD on a genuine parse miss (R5, re-verified this cycle) and must not be keyed to lead-in prose (standing T-012 hazard).

CYCLE 28: ATTEMPTED AND REJECTED AT THE GATE; attempts 0 -> 1, work REVERTED, item stays todo. The obvious fix -- scan every '### ' heading, strip backticks, take the FIRST whose text carries both the --list token and the word 'behaviour' -- passed all 22 gate checks including both acceptance halves, both discriminators and every loudness check, and was still rejected. Why, measured in .swarm/runs/cycle-028-probe-B4.{js,txt}: FIRST-MATCH-WINS lets an earlier '### ' heading carrying both tokens capture the section, and the consequence is a SILENT HOLE rather than the loud rejection this family has always produced. P3 is the decisive cell -- an earlier decoy heading whose section carries a CORRECT-looking `<text> - <author>` literal, with the REAL section's literal mutated to something FALSE, passes at 73/73/0. P4 proves HEAD CATCHES that same input at 73/72/1. So the fix traded a loud false rejection for a wrong README going green, which is backwards on this repo's own stated standard and strictly worse than leaving T-021 open. Contrast gate check B4/B4b, which found the surface, and P1 (decoy section with NO literal) which is merely loud at HEADING-PARSE -- the hole only opens when the decoy section carries a plausible literal. P5 shows the shape is narrow: BOTH tokens are required in the decoy heading, so a heading like '### --list-only mode' alone is harmless. NEXT ATTEMPT must disambiguate rather than take the first match. Candidate shapes, none yet measured: require the heading text to carry --list as a STANDALONE token (not the --list- prefix of a longer flag); prefer the heading whose section actually contains a `<text>...<author>` literal and assert LOUD if two or more do; or keep first-match but assert loud when more than one candidate heading exists. Whichever is chosen must keep A1/A2/D1/D2/L1/L2 and add a check that P3 goes RED. The full gate is reusable at .swarm/runs/cycle-028-verify-T-021.js.

items.title: Let the band-heading count parser tolerate a lead-in phrase before the "N tags" count
items.acceptance: Rewording a band heading so a descriptive phrase precedes the count -- e.g. `Well-populated: 4 tags carry 5+ entries each.` or `Mid-range: 12 tags land in the 2-4 band.`, both of which leave every stated number TRUE and every table row untouched -- leaves the suite GREEN, while a WRONG stated count under that same reworded heading still FAILS. Proven twice per L-029.
items.notes: Source: conductor gate check R3.GREEN, cycle 24 -- .swarm/runs/cycle-024-verify-T-019.txt. MEASURED, not suspected, and the attribution was measured too rather than assumed (.swarm/runs/cycle-024-probe-R3.txt): the test 'README band table headings must state the correct count of tags in their band' parses the stated count with /^\s*(\d+)\s+tags\b/, anchored to the START of the heading line, so any lead-in prefix makes the parse fail. Rewording either heading fails the suite at 1 test. THE ATTRIBUTION PROBE IS THE POINT: the identical rewording fails identically against HEAD's test file, which has no T-019 test at all (72 tests, same single failing test), and the T-019 assertion stays green under all three rewording variants. So this is a PRE-EXISTING fragility that cycle 24's gate happened to surface, NOT something T-019 introduced -- recorded that way because the tempting reading of a red gate check is that the item under test caused it. IMPORTANT, and why this is LOW value rather than a T-012 repeat: the guard does NOT go quiet. Its own assert fires with 'could not parse a leading "N tags" count from band heading ... -- this claim must fail loud, not pass silently, when it cannot be parsed', which is a message T-014's builder wrote deliberately for exactly this case. So a maintainer who trips it is told precisely what happened. Same safe-direction classification as T-018 (cycle 20), T-020 (cycle 22) and T-021 (cycle 23); this is now the fourth member of that family, and the recurrence is itself worth a wrap-up lesson -- every guard this run has built keys some extraction to a positional or literal anchor in prose. Fix shape: bind the count to the word 'tags' anywhere in the heading rather than to line start, while keeping the band-bound digits ('5+', '2-4') distinguishable from the count digit -- note the two are already parsed by separate regexes, so the risk is a heading where the FIRST 'N tags' is not the band count. Whatever is chosen must still fail LOUD on a genuine parse miss, and must not be keyed to lead-in prose (standing T-012 hazard).
items.evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-025-verify-T-022.txt — 34/35 conductor gate checks. Both shipped band headings reworded with a lead-in now stay GREEN (A1/A2), and three rewordings the builder never saw also stay green (A3 em-dash aside, A4 digit-bearing lead-in, A5 both headings at once with the count AFTER the band token). Each is attributed: the identical reword against pre-fix HEAD is rejected at 73/72/1 naming this guard alone. RED half upgraded from accidental to real — a wrong count under a reworded heading now fails on COUNT-MISMATCH (A7/A8/A9), where at baseline it only failed because the parse died first. Clause 4 holds: A10 (no count phrase at all) and A11 (only candidate overlaps the band token) both assert LOUD. Discriminators a hardcoded fix could not pass: R1 promoted `yagni` 1->2 IN THE CORPUS with a consistently updated AND reworded README (green 73/73) against a stale half that fails at 73/68/5 naming this guard; R2 restructured into a THREE-band reworded layout this repo has never had (green 73/73), then put a wrong count on the MIDDLE band (fails naming this guard alone, COUNT-MISMATCH). test_cmd on the real tree, run by the conductor: 73/73/0.

items.title: Decide the band heading whose LEAD-IN carries its own "N tags" count: harden or document as BOUNDARY
items.acceptance: FIRST classify, then act (SPEC I-2 explicitly allows a BOUNDARY survivor to be documented rather than hardened). If HOLE: a band heading whose lead-in contains a true "N tags" phrase before the band's own count -- e.g. `Of 37 tags, 4 tags carry 5+ entries each.` -- leaves the suite GREEN, while a wrong band count under that same heading still FAILS on a count comparison, proven twice. If BOUNDARY: the ambiguity is stated in a comment at the extraction site naming the exact heading shape that is out of scope and why prose alone cannot resolve it, and no test is added. Either way the guard must keep failing LOUD.
items.notes: CYCLE 27 NOTE: still the right shape. T-018 landed this cycle WITHOUT narrowing a prose anchor -- its locator was already structural (the `| Tag | Count |` header + separator row) and the fix removed an adjacency requirement -- so T-018 is not a sixth member of this family, and the family remains T-020/T-021/T-023 (see T-024, filed cycle 27, for the re-shape). || Source: conductor gate residual probe, cycle 25 -- .swarm/runs/cycle-025-verify-T-022.txt, final section. MEASURED, not suspected: rewriting the 5+ heading to `Of 37 tags, 4 tags carry 5+ entries each.` -- every number TRUE (the corpus does have 37 distinct tags), every row untouched -- fails at 73/72/1 naming this guard alone, with reason COUNT-MISMATCH: the parser takes the FIRST "N tags" match that does not overlap the band token, which is `37 tags`, and then reports 'states 37 tags, but the corpus has 4'. THIS IS THE FIFTH MEMBER of the family T-018 (c20), T-020 (c22), T-021 (c23), T-022 (c24) -- every guard this run has built keys some extraction to a positional or literal anchor in prose, and each fix has narrowed the anchor rather than removed it. That recurrence is a wrap-up lesson in its own right and is more valuable than this item. WHY THIS MAY BE A BOUNDARY RATHER THAN A HOLE, and why it is priority 6 rather than 7: a heading containing two true "N tags" phrases is genuinely ambiguous to a machine -- there is no ground truth in the prose saying which one is the band count. The three earlier members were unambiguous reformattings; this one is not. It also fails LOUD and readably (the message quotes the heading and both numbers), so a maintainer who trips it is told what happened. Hardening it by, say, preferring the LAST candidate or the one nearest the band token would trade this false rejection for a different one, and that trade must be argued before it is made.

items.title: Re-shape the prose-anchored extractions in readme-tags.test.js to read structure instead
items.acceptance: The extractions behind T-020 (Attribution counts), T-021 (the --list behaviour section locator) and T-023 (a band heading whose lead-in carries its own "N tags" count) derive their values from document STRUCTURE -- tables, rows, headings-as-headings, tokens -- rather than from a position or literal inside an English sentence, and all three of those items' measured false-rejection cases go green without any of the guards going quiet. Every existing kill must still be a kill, proven per L-029, and every parse miss must still fail LOUD.
items.notes:
Source: cycle-25 standing decision (state.json decisions[], cycle 25) converted into an actionable item at cycle 27, per the cycle-26 handoff's instruction to FILE the re-shape as an M item if it is the right answer but does not fit gear 1. It is, and it does not. WHY AN UMBRELLA RATHER THAN THREE MORE NARROWINGS: every README guard this run built extracts a number by anchoring to a position or a literal in prose, and every fix so far (T-012, T-018, T-020, T-021, T-022, T-023) has narrowed the anchor rather than removed it. The failure direction has been safe every time -- these guards reject a correct README loudly, they never pass a wrong one silently -- but a maintainer's cheapest escape from a false rejection is DELETING the guard, so the cumulative risk is the whole family going at once. A seventh narrowing does not reduce that risk; changing what the extractions read does. HONEST SCOPE NOTE, so this is not mistaken for a bigger claim: T-018 is NOT part of this family and was correctly fixed narrowly at cycle 27 -- its locator was already structural (the `| Tag | Count |` header row plus the separator row) and the defect was an adjacency requirement, not a prose anchor. Band-bound digits (`5+`, `2-4`) are also fine to read from a heading: they carry mathematical meaning, which the cycle-25 finding explicitly permits. The target is prose WORDING as an anchor, nothing else.

UNREACHABLE FOR THE REST OF THIS RUN (recorded cycle 27, not a judgment on the item): gear is structurally pinned at 1 because the weekly window resets at 1786942799, after stop_at 1786879464, and gear 1 admits S-effort builds only. This item is M-effort. Left todo for the next run on a healthier window.

items.title: Decide the band heading separated from its table by prose: harden or document as BOUNDARY
items.acceptance: FIRST classify, then act (SPEC I-2 explicitly allows a BOUNDARY survivor to be documented rather than hardened). If HOLE: a band heading separated from its `| Tag | Count |` table by an ordinary sentence -- e.g. `4 tags have a robust pool (5+ entries):` / blank / `See the table below.` / blank / the table -- leaves the suite GREEN, while a row deletion under that same layout still FAILS, proven twice. If BOUNDARY: the limit is stated in a comment at the extraction site naming the exact layout that is out of scope and why widening the scan is the more dangerous trade, and no test is added. Either way the guard must keep failing LOUD.
items.notes: Source: conductor gate check A12, cycle 27 -- .swarm/runs/cycle-027-verify-T-018.txt. MEASURED, not suspected: with T-018's fix in place, `4 tags have a robust pool (5+ entries):` followed by a blank line, the sentence `See the table below.`, another blank line and then the real table fails at 73/72/1, naming the T-019 union guard. NOT A REGRESSION -- it failed at HEAD too, because HEAD required strict adjacency and any interposed content broke the parse. T-018 widened the tolerated gap to blank lines only, which is exactly what its own constraint set asked for. WHY THIS IS PROBABLY A BOUNDARY, and why it is priority 8 rather than 7: the fix that would close it is to scan PAST non-blank content looking for a table, and that is precisely the mis-attachment hazard T-018 was told to avoid -- gate check A11 confirms the current conservative scan does not let a decoy line carrying a band-shaped digit token steal a later table, and a widened scan would put that property back at risk. So closing this trades a loud false rejection for a possible silent mis-parse, which is the wrong direction on this repo's own stated standard. It also fails LOUD and readably. The honest exit may well be a comment at the extraction site rather than a test. This is the same classify-before-hardening shape as T-023 and is filed the same way. Lower value than T-023 because a sentence wedged between a heading and its own table is a less likely edit than a reworded heading.
